Question: Organization name
What we are asking for, and why: The trading name of the business exactly as customers know it. If you trade under more than one name, put the main one here.

Question: Industry
What we are asking for, and why: What kind of business this is. Pick the single closest match from the Industry list. This only classifies the business for reporting; it does not change how anything works.

Question: Primary markets
What we are asking for, and why: The countries where your customers actually are. Pick every country you sell to today, not ones you hope to enter later.

Question: Reporting currency
What we are asking for, and why: The currency you want every budget and performance report shown in. Usually the currency your bank account is in.

Question: Legal or operating identity
What we are asking for, and why: The registered company or trade licence name, if it is different from the name customers see. Leave blank if they are the same.

Question: Value proposition
What we are asking for, and why: In a few sentences: why does a customer choose you over the place next door? Write it in plain language, the way you would explain it to a new employee.
Example: Home-style Emirati food made fresh daily, delivered hot across Dubai in under 40 minutes.

Question: Branchless operation
What we are asking for, and why: Answer Yes only if the business has no physical location at all — for example a cloud kitchen with no customer-facing site, or a purely online business. If you answer Yes you can leave the Branches question blank.

Question: Branches
What we are asking for, and why: Every physical location you operate, one per line. Use the name your team uses for it. Required unless you answered Yes to 'Branchless operation' above.

Question: Operating hours
What we are asking for, and why: The normal weekly opening hours customers can rely on. Fill these in on the 'Opening hours' sheet, not here. Public holidays and one-off closures do not belong here.
Allowed answers: Times in 24-hour format, on the hour or half hour

Question: Service areas
What we are asking for, and why: The delivery zones, districts, or regions you cover, one per line. Skip this if you do not deliver or travel to customers.

Question: Capacity and constraints
What we are asking for, and why: The practical limits on how much business you can take. Seats, kitchen throughput at peak, delivery drivers available, staffing gaps on certain days. This stops us from driving demand you cannot serve.
Example: 60 covers indoors. Kitchen handles about 25 delivery orders an hour at peak. Only one driver after 10pm.

Question: Products or services
What we are asking for, and why: Your headline products or services, one per line — the ones that matter most to sales. You do not need the full menu here; a full menu or price list can be sent as a file instead (see section 10).
Example:
Chicken machboos
Lamb ouzi
Mixed grill platter

Question: Categories
What we are asking for, and why: The broad groups your offer falls into. Pick every one that applies.
Allowed answers: See 'Choice lists' → Product or service categories

Question: Pricing currency
What we are asking for, and why: The currency your prices are set in. Usually the same as the reporting currency.

Question: Average order value
What we are asking for, and why: What a typical single order or booking is worth, before any discount. Write it the normal way, with decimals — for example 45.00. If it varies a lot by channel, give the overall average and note the variation in the next question.
Allowed answers: A number in the pricing currency above

Question: Availability and modifiers
What we are asking for, and why: Anything that changes what is on sale: seasonal items, weekend-only dishes, add-ons and extras, items that regularly sell out, minimum order sizes.
Example: Seafood specials on Fridays only. Family platters need 2 hours' notice. Add-ons: extra rice, extra sauce.

Question: Owned and marketplace channels
What we are asking for, and why: Every place customers can find or buy from you today. Pick all that apply. Do not include channels you plan to open later.
Allowed answers: See 'Choice lists' → Sales and marketing channels

Question: Public profile links
What we are asking for, and why: The public web address of each channel above, one per line. Full links are best. Never put passwords or login details here — access is granted separately through a secure connection flow.

Question: Account ownership
What we are asking for, and why: Who owns the logins for the accounts above — your business, the agency, or a mix. This matters if the working relationship ever changes.

Question: Conversion tracking
What we are asking for, and why: Whether you can currently see which marketing actually produced a sale. Only pick 'Connected and verified' if somebody has checked the numbers are correct end to end — over-stating this makes every later result unreliable.

Question: Historical metrics
What we are asking for, and why: Which past figures you can actually produce from a report or export. Pick only what you can evidence — not what could be estimated. It is completely fine to pick just one or two.
Example: Revenue; Orders or transactions; Marketing spend

Question: Measurement period
What we are asking for, and why: The months these figures cover — a finished window, not one still running. Write the first and last month as YYYY-MM. Both months are included.

Question: Currency
What we are asking for, and why: The currency the figures above are stated in.

Question: Source and quality
What we are asking for, and why: Where these numbers came from. This tells us how much weight to put on them.
Allowed answers: See 'Choice lists' → Source of the performance figures

Question: Source notes
What we are asking for, and why: Anything that would mislead somebody reading these figures cold: months with missing data, whether refunds and cancellations are taken out, a branch that opened mid-period, VAT included or not.
Example: Revenue excludes VAT. Refunds are not deducted. March is missing — the POS was replaced that month.

Question: The figures themselves
What we are asking for, and why: Please attach or send the actual numbers as an export or spreadsheet rather than retyping them here — an original report is always more reliable than a re-keyed one. List what you are sending in the 'Upload notes' question in section 10.

Question: What each order costs
What we are asking for, and why: What a single order costs you before profit — commission, ingredients, packaging, delivery, payment fees. Fill this in on the 'Cost structure' sheet, one row per cost. Price what you know and leave the rest blank; nothing is guessed on your behalf. Where a cost genuinely does not apply, write 0 rather than leaving it empty — that is a real answer and a useful one.

Question: In force from
What we are asking for, and why: The date these cost figures started applying. If your marketplace commission changed in June, use the date of the change. Earlier months keep the older figures, so a change now never rewrites a profit figure you have already seen.

Question: Source and caveats
What we are asking for, and why: Anything that qualifies the cost figures: contract references, rates that drop once you pass a volume tier, different commissions per marketplace, costs nobody knows yet.
Example: Talabat commission drops to 22% above AED 150k a month. Packaging cost is from the March supplier invoice.

Question: Customer segments
What we are asking for, and why: The customer groups that genuinely exist in your business today. Pick all that apply.

Question: First-party data availability
What we are asking for, and why: Where you hold customer contact details that belong to your business. 'First-party' simply means data you collected yourself, rather than data a platform holds about your customers.
Allowed answers: See 'Choice lists' → First-party customer data you hold
Example: POS history; Email list; Loyalty programme

Question: Consent confirmation source
What we are asking for, and why: Whether your customers agreed to be contacted with marketing, and who is confirming that. This is a legal statement, so it must come from a person — never a system, and never an assumption. 'Unknown' is a perfectly acceptable answer and is far better than a hopeful one.

Question: Retention and contactability constraints
What we are asking for, and why: Any rules limiting how you may contact customers: how long you keep records, how opt-outs are handled, channels you are not allowed to use, quiet hours, or contract terms with a marketplace that forbid contacting its customers.
Example: We delete customer records after 24 months. Marketplace customers must not be contacted directly. No SMS after 9pm.

Question: Brand voice
What we are asking for, and why: How your brand should sound to a customer. Pick the traits that fit; two or three is usually enough.

Question: Languages
What we are asking for, and why: Every language you communicate with customers in. Pick all that apply.

Question: Asset sources
What we are asking for, and why: Where your approved logos, photos, and brand guidelines live, one per line. A shared folder link or a description of who holds them is fine.
Example:
Brand guidelines: Google Drive → Marketing → Brand
Food photography: Dropbox → Shoots 2025

Question: Claims and approvals
What we are asking for, and why: Anything we must not say, and who signs off on what we do say. Wording your industry regulates, health or origin claims you cannot make, competitor comparisons you avoid — and the name and role of the person who approves public copy.
Example: Never claim 'organic' — we are not certified. All halal wording must be approved by Fatima (Operations Manager) before publishing.

Question: Measurable goals
What we are asking for, and why: What you want this to achieve, one goal per line. Each goal needs a number and a date, otherwise nobody can tell later whether it worked. 'Grow the business' cannot be measured; 'increase repeat orders by 15% by December 2026' can.
Example:
Increase repeat orders by 15% by December 2026
Bring delivery customer acquisition cost below AED 25 by Q3

Question: Baseline status
What we are asking for, and why: Whether you know the current 'before' number for those goals. Without a baseline nobody can prove improvement later — so if it is an estimate, say so.

Question: Budget currency
What we are asking for, and why: The currency your marketing budget is set in.

Question: Monthly budget
What we are asking for, and why: How much you are prepared to spend on marketing each month, in the currency above. Write it the normal way, with decimals — for example 2500.00. This is a ceiling, not a target to spend.
Allowed answers: A number in the budget currency above

Question: Approval mode
What we are asking for, and why: How much the platform may do without asking you first. Whichever you pick, anything that spends money or publishes publicly as your brand always waits for a human to approve it.

Question: Hard and soft constraints
What we are asking for, and why: The lines we must not cross and the ones we should avoid, one per line. Minimum prices, discounts you will never run, competitors you will not name, imagery you will not use, days you do not promote.
Example:
Never discount below 20% margin
No alcohol imagery
No promotions during Ramadan daylight hours

Question: Available integrations and files
What we are asking for, and why: Everything the agency can be given access to, or that you can export and send. Pick all that apply. Access itself is granted later through each provider's own secure login flow — never by sending a password.
Allowed answers: See 'Choice lists' → Data sources and integrations
Example: POS export; Google Business Profile; Meta Business Suite; Menu or catalog file

Question: Permission gaps
What we are asking for, and why: Anything above that you cannot grant access to yet, and why, one per line. Each gap becomes a task somebody can chase, so naming it here saves a week later.
Example:
No admin access to the Meta page — the previous agency holds it
Talabat portal login sits with head office

Question: Upload notes
What we are asking for, and why: Which files you are sending with this sheet, and which ones are still to come. Accepted file types are CSV, TXT, PDF, PNG and JPEG, up to 50 MB each.
Example: Attached: menu-2026.pdf, pos-export-2025.csv. Still to come: supplier cost sheet from accounts.

Question: Files to send with this sheet
What we are asking for, and why: Attach whatever supports your answers — menu or price list, POS export, marketplace statements, brand guidelines, a recent invoice showing packaging cost. Original exports beat retyped figures every time.
Allowed answers: CSV, TXT, PDF, PNG or JPEG, up to 50 MB each

Question: Nothing to fill in here
What we are asking for, and why: This last step is ours, not yours. Once your answers are in, the platform scores how ready the business is, lists anything still missing, and a named person on the agency side confirms the review. If something critical is still open, we will come back to you with a short, specific list rather than this whole sheet again.
